scope: Deployed loopback API over retained 9,249,545-row cut; closed-loop public read traffic only

profile.route_selection: round-robin, rotated per client, equal four-route mix; next request begins after response

limits: Pilot profile, not an accepted SLA or production demand specification
Warm cache after sequential reference requests
No concurrent transformation, initial bulk insertion, worker failure or source network failure in this trial

Resources cover pinned supervisor descendants, the entire native :5432 postmaster descendant tree and the load generator. Private bytes are sampled; working sets share pages. Other PostgreSQL clusters are excluded.

Native postmaster creation agrees with PID file; pg_postmaster_start_time differs by 56.246 s and is recorded independently, with no cause attributed. Cluster identity is also bound through SQL backend ancestry; both timestamps stay unchanged.

Three initial observer runs were stopped by fail-closed guards and preserved separately; the first saved only an initial checkpoint. The third detected a stale parent PID link. Invalid parent-age branches are excluded and recorded; a changed root identity still fails immediately. This run permits at most eight acquisition attempts, records discarded churn and never counts incomplete readings as stable samples.

Root PID and creation stamps are pinned; both process inventories must match per sample. No continuous peak guarantee between samples. CPU and I/O counters are cumulative per process, not disk-only physical I/O or interval utilization.
